summary: Legacy R script fits GLM1 of the Noll/Salzmann/Wuthrich (2018) freMTPL2 case study: a Poisson claim-frequency GLM (log link) with offset log(Exposure) on a 90% learn sample. Features: VehPowerGLM (factor, VehPower capped at 9), VehAgeGLM (3 classes, ref '2'), DrivAgeGLM (7 age bands, ref '5'), BonusMalusGLM (capped at 150, continuous), VehBrand (factor, ref B1), VehGas (factor), DensityGLM (log Density), Region (factor, ref R24), AreaGLM (Area A..F as integer 1..6). 49 coefficients, converged in 6 IRLS iterations.

preprocessing.description: Read CSV; both double and single quotes are quote characters, so surrounding single quotes on Area, VehBrand, VehGas, Region are removed. check.names=TRUE (column names already syntactic). Strings stay character.
Cap exposure at 1 year (enters the offset).
Integer code of Area factor (levels sorted A..F -> 1..6), used as continuous.
VehPower capped at 9, then factor with numeric-sorted levels 4..9 (ref 4).

preprocessing.r_code:
VehAgeGLM <- cbind(c(0:110), c(1, rep(2, 10), rep(3, 100)))
dat$VehAgeGLM <- as.factor(VehAgeGLM[dat$VehAge + 1, 2])
dat[, "VehAgeGLM"] <- relevel(dat[, "VehAgeGLM"], ref = "2")
preprocessing.description: Lookup table: VehAge 0 -> 1, 1..10 -> 2, 11..110 -> 3; factor then relevel reference to '2' (levels 2,1,3). Positional column 2 of the lookup matrix is the class code; dat[, "VehAgeGLM"] is a named reference.

preprocessing.r_code:
DrivAgeGLM <- cbind(c(18:100), c(rep(1, 21 - 18), rep(2, 26 - 21), rep(3, 31 - 26), rep(4, 41 - 31), rep(5, 51 - 41), rep(6, 71 - 51), rep(7, 101 - 71)))
dat$DrivAgeGLM <- as.factor(DrivAgeGLM[dat$DrivAge - 17, 2])
dat[, "DrivAgeGLM"] <- relevel(dat[, "DrivAgeGLM"], ref = "5")
preprocessing.description: Lookup table: DrivAge 18-20 -> 1, 21-25 -> 2, 26-30 -> 3, 31-40 -> 4, 41-50 -> 5, 51-70 -> 6, 71-100 -> 7; factor then relevel reference to '5' (levels 5,1,2,3,4,6,7). Protected attribute (age).

preprocessing.r_code:
dat$VehBrand <- relevel(as.factor(dat$VehBrand), ref = "B1")
dat$Region <- relevel(as.factor(dat$Region), ref = "R24")
dat$VehGas <- as.factor(dat$VehGas)
preprocessing.description: Factors with string-sorted levels; VehBrand reference B1, Region reference R24, VehGas reference Diesel. Levels taken from model$xlevels.

model.formula: ClaimNb ~ VehPowerGLM + VehAgeGLM + DrivAgeGLM + BonusMalusGLM + VehBrand + VehGas + DensityGLM + Region + AreaGLM, offset = log(Exposure)

randomness: set.seed(100); ll <- sample(1:nrow(dat), round(0.9*nrow(dat))) gives a 90/10 learn/test split. Not re-implemented: the frozen split from the R capture (model/reference/split.csv) is supplied by the harness (R-RNG-01).
risks: GOV-01: DrivAge (age, protected characteristic) enters the model via DrivAgeGLM bands; migrated faithfully, needs actuarial justification (Equality Act 2010 Sch.3 para 20A) and fairness review.
AreaGLM uses the integer code of a factor (as.integer(factor(Area))): depends on level sorting; treats an ordinal as linear.

Hard-coded lookup tables: VehAge > 110 or DrivAge outside 18..100 would make R fail (subscript out of bounds) or produce wrong rows; Python maps such values to NaN (no prediction). No such values affected the R run.
Data error treatments (ClaimNb capped at 4, Exposure capped at 1) are judgemental and applied before the split.
Region / VehBrand levels absent in future data, or new levels, cannot be scored (NaN in Python; R predict would error).
Reproducibility of the split depends on R's RNG (sample.kind Rejection, R >= 3.6); split frozen from capture.
Source is a reconstruction of the published case study, not the original notebook.
